messages:
Alyssa: ran a quick nsys on the dedicated pool during the 200k req/min test, attaching the condensed top kernels by total time. looks like a long tail of small kernels + a couple huge hot kernels. can someone sanity-check these suspects?
Noah: :eyes: paste the top list pls, but my hunch is kv_lookup or MHA_fwd. those are usually loud.
Alyssa: pasted snippet: 
```
1) MHA_fwd_kernel            total_ms  1240.5  (37%)
2) kv_lookup_async           total_ms   760.2  (22%)
3) prefix_scan_kernel        total_ms   340.1   (10%)
4) softmax_stable            total_ms   210.4    (6%)
5) merge_batched_outputs     total_ms   190.7    (6%)
... many small memcpy and atomic kernels ~15% combined
```
Alyssa: trace window was 120s, batch size distribution peaked at 8 and 64 depending on route.
Marina: interesting that prefix_scan is that high — could be our kv-cache eviction path. are we seeing lots of cache misses?
perf-bot: auto-report: average SM util across GPUs=41%, warp_efficiency=79%, achieved_occupancy=0.58, kernel_launch_overhead spikes correlated with small memcpy bursts.
Devon: try this nvprof snippet for per-kernel occupancy: 
```bash
nvprof --metrics achieved_occupancy,sm_efficiency,inst_executed per_kernel_trace.nvvp
```
Devon: also run nsys with --sample=cpu to correlate host stalls, sometimes the batching thread starves the GPU.
Noah: MHA_fwd looks heavy — is it using our fused attention or falling back to naive path?
Alyssa: runtime reported fused path, but kernel name is the generic MHA_fwd_kernel: could be switching kernels per sequence length. I'll grep the nvtx regions.
Marina: if KV lookup async is 22% and SM util is 41% we might be IO bound or hitting warp divergence in the lookup kernel. check branch divergence metric.
Devon: small follow-up: run with --trace=cuda,nvtx and look for long gaps between kernel launches in perfetto; that will reveal batching inefficiency.
Alyssa: plan: run focused 30s nsys sampling on the two heavy kernels with full metrics (achieved_occupancy, divergent_branch, memory_throughput). will post results.
Noah: if occupancy low + high mem throughput => poor memory coalescing, consider reordering key layout or using vectorized loads.
Marina: also experiment reducing micro-batch size to see if launch overhead beats better utilization — might be a tradeoff for short seqs.
Alyssa: noted. thanks all. tagging next actions: @Devon run nvprof occupancy, @Noah test vectorized loads patch, @Marina run cache-miss profile on kv path. I'll re-run nsys and post timeline. :thumbsup:
